title: Regular-functorial normalized resolution rules on quasi-excellent rational inputs
statement:
An input is a reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $X$ over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-exc-excellent-ring], with its rational structure morphism and no finite-type or separation restriction. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence admitting a finite affine Noetherian cover. Normal inputs are the subtype for which every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; the empty scheme and finite disjoint unions are allowed.

A based normalized resolution tower consists of a finite normalized blowup tower, with its ordered ideal centers [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], [def-trf-normalized-blowup], an isomorphism of its first level to its input, coherent centers [pqf-def-coherent] with nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes [def-per-normalized-tower-descent-data], and regular last level [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its structural maps are the recursive composites to level zero followed by the initial isomorphism.

A contracted regular pullback comparison of two such towers over $h:Y\to X$ [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] consists of the full recursively pulled-back normalized tower, its isomorphism of level zero with $Y$, maps to the original tower that commute with arrows and identify its center ideals with their extended ideals, and a cartesian square at every level [def-pc-fibre-product]. It includes an ordered contraction [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] to the tower on $Y$, compatible with the initial isomorphisms; every unit-center stage in the pulled tower is an isomorphism and the contraction deletes exactly those unit-center stages, preserving the other extended ideals in order. A proper invertible center is retained even if its blowup is an isomorphism. The comparison level map is the inverse contraction isomorphism followed by the full pullback map.

For a specified family of input schemes, a regular-functorial normalized resolution rule assigns one such resolution tower to each member and one such comparison to every regular morphism between members. The empty scheme has a length-zero tower. Identity and composition hold on both the ordered contraction indices and the actual comparison level maps (transporting the source along the equality of indices). A surjective regular morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism] has an injective contraction index, so deletes no stage. The two input families of interest are all reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent rational schemes and their normal members.
